place.title: Place {ref} (active buzzer module)
place.text: Push the buzzer module {ref}'s 3 pins into column f, one pin per row: GND into hole {hole.gnd}, I/O into {hole.io} and VCC into {hole.vcc}. The buzzer faces up.
place.tip: Read the labels printed next to the pins: GND, I/O, VCC. If yours are in another order, follow the labels, not the picture. An active buzzer usually has a sealed top; a passive one shows its circuit board underneath.

why: {ref} is an active buzzer: it has its own tone inside and beeps at one pitch while it is switched on. This module is on while its I/O pin is LOW, so the program keeps the pin HIGH when it should be quiet.

wire.ground: This connects {ref}'s GND pin to ground.
wire.power: This powers {ref} from 3.3 V, not 5 V: the module is on while I/O is LOW, and from 5 V the Pico's 3.3 V HIGH couldn't switch it off.
wire.out: {pin} switches {ref}: LOW (0) beeps, HIGH (1) is quiet.
